headline: Indy's sound is brass and heritage, and the Pacers already have the soundtrack.
summary: Indianapolis music runs on heritage and brass. The Indiana Avenue jazz clubs sat a few blocks from Oscar Robertson's Crispus Attucks title teams, and the city is now the center of American marching music. Its real anthem is a 1917 song, "Back Home Again in Indiana." This season the sound fits Haliburton's return and the white, royal blue and gold Moments Mixtape City Edition.

insights.title: Jazz and basketball shared the Avenue
insights.detail: In the 1940s and 50s, Indiana Avenue's clubs produced Wes Montgomery, Freddie Hubbard, J.J. Johnson and David Baker. A few blocks away, Oscar Robertson's Crispus Attucks Tigers won the 1955 and 1956 state titles, the first all-Black school in the nation to win an open state championship. Highways and the IUPUI campus later cleared much of the neighborhood. The 1927 Madam Walker theatre survives as its anchor.
insights.implication: Nowhere else do Indy's music and basketball histories share a street, so this is the market's strongest heritage story. Make it with the Madam Walker Legacy Center and the Crispus Attucks Museum, and credit and pay both. Never turn it into jazz-age nostalgia graphics.

insights.title: The real anthem is a 1917 song
insights.detail: "Back Home Again in Indiana" is sung before every Indy 500, and Jim Nabors sang it for four decades, through 2014. Louis Armstrong's All Stars often opened with it, and Charlie Parker's bebop standard "Donna Lee" is built on its chord changes. The 1917 composition is in the U.S. public domain.
insights.implication: With Haliburton back from his Achilles tear, "Back Home Again" is the obvious line for the home opener and the bounce-back season. The lyric and melody are free to use. Specific recordings (Nabors' included) and every Indy 500 mark are not.

insights.title: Indianapolis is the marching-arts capital
insights.detail: Drum Corps International, Music for All (Bands of America) and the Percussive Arts Society are all headquartered here. In August the DCI World Championships fill Lucas Oil Stadium, blocks from the Fieldhouse. The ISSMA state finals, BOA Grand Nationals and PASIC follow in November. Suburban programs like Carmel and Avon are perennial national powers, and pep bands still drive the small-town gym.
insights.implication: Drumline is the market's native sound of sport. Build band-jacket silhouettes, gauntlet cuffs and brass hardware into product. Hire Indiana high-school drumlines to play launches, and send the proceeds to band programs.

insights.title: The R&B line runs from Carr to Babyface
insights.detail: An Indianapolis duo cut Leroy Carr's 1928 "How Long, How Long Blues," and the Ink Spots formed here in the early 1930s. The line runs on to Kenneth "Babyface" Edmonds, a North Central High School alum whose brothers formed After 7. Babyface is the city's marquee living music name.
insights.implication: A premium "Naptown Soul" lifestyle story (satin, suede, monochrome navy) suits this lineage better than hype graphics. A Babyface collaboration would be the big get, on his team's terms.

insights.title: Two Indianas: the Avenue and the county seat
insights.detail: Pacers fandom is statewide. Rural Indiana's soundtrack is John Mellencamp's heartland rock (he's a Seymour native; think "Small Town" and "Pink Houses"). It's also Bill Monroe's Bean Blossom bluegrass festival in Brown County, held every June since 1967. Richmond's Gennett Records cut King Oliver's band with a young Louis Armstrong in 1923, and Hoagy Carmichael's "Stardust" in 1927.
insights.implication: Statewide product should cite named Indiana songs, towns and studios, not generic barns-and-cornfields Midwest imagery. Mellencamp's lyrics and likeness need licensing.

insights.title: The Pacers' own sound: "Boom Baby!"
insights.detail: Bobby "Slick" Leonard coached the ABA Pacers to titles in 1970, 1972 and 1973. He then called Pacers threes on the radio for decades with "Boom Baby!", the franchise's best-loved piece of audio. The Moments Mixtape City Edition (white, royal blue and gold) is reportedly returning for 2026-27, and its name already frames team history as a track list.
insights.implication: Nike co-owns the uniform's metaphor, so extend it. Use cassette J-card graphics, a "Side B" lifestyle drop and a mix commissioned from Indy DJs. Use "Boom Baby!" as the audio hook in launch content once the team and Leonard's estate clear it.

places.name: Madam Walker Legacy Center
places.why: Madam C.J. Walker's company built this 1927 terra-cotta theatre. It's the surviving anchor of the Avenue's jazz era and the essential partner for any Avenue story.

places.name: Crispus Attucks Museum
places.why: It tells the story of the 1955-56 Attucks champions, who shared a neighborhood with the Avenue's jazz clubs. That bridges the music and basketball lenses.

places.name: The Jazz Kitchen
places.why: Indy's flagship jazz room since 1994, where local and touring players keep the Montgomery-Hubbard lineage going.

places.name: Chatterbox Jazz Club
places.why: A tiny, decades-old late-night jazz bar. Plugged-in locals rate it above any downtown tourist stop.

places.name: Old National Centre (Murat Theatre and Egyptian Room)
places.why: The Murat Shrine complex is Indy's mid-size touring stage. The Egyptian Room is a rite-of-passage hip-hop and rock room.

places.name: The Vogue
places.why: A 1938 movie house, and Broad Ripple's anchor rock and dance club since the late 1970s.

places.name: HI-FI Indy
places.why: The small independent room at the center of Fountain Square's local and indie bills.

places.name: Luna Music
places.why: Indy's best-known independent record store, and the natural home for numbered, record-style product drops.

places.name: Lucas Oil Stadium
places.why: Hosts the DCI World Championships, BOA Grand Nationals and ISSMA state finals, a short walk from Gainbridge Fieldhouse.

places.name: Rhythm! Discovery Center
places.why: The Percussive Arts Society's hands-on drum museum, a ready-made partner for drumline product stories.

people.name: Wes Montgomery
people.why: Indy's most influential musician. He worked factory shifts by day and played Avenue clubs at night, and his thumb-picked octaves changed jazz guitar.

people.name: Freddie Hubbard
people.why: An Indianapolis native who came up with the Montgomery brothers before becoming a Blue Note star. He's part of the Avenue's export line.

people.name: David Baker
people.why: A Crispus Attucks alum and Avenue player who founded Indiana University's jazz studies program, linking the Avenue to Bloomington.

people.name: Leroy Carr
people.why: With guitarist Scrapper Blackwell he made "How Long, How Long Blues" (1928), which put Indianapolis on the early blues map.

people.name: Kenneth 'Babyface' Edmonds
people.why: The city's marquee living music name: born in Indianapolis, a North Central High School alum, with brothers who formed After 7.

people.name: John Mellencamp
people.why: A Seymour native based near Bloomington and a devoted Indiana hoops fan, he's the voice of the small-town Indiana that fills Pacers fandom.

people.name: Bobby 'Slick' Leonard
people.role: ABA-champion Pacers coach and longtime radio analyst (1932-2021)
people.why: His "Boom Baby!" three-point call is the franchise's signature sound.

people.name: Music for All
people.role: Indianapolis nonprofit that runs Bands of America
people.why: Its Grand National Championships at Lucas Oil each November are the marching-band world's Final Four. Its programs are a natural home for proceeds.

moments.name: IHSAA boys' basketball state finals
moments.why: Hoosier Hysteria peaks with small-town pep bands playing fight songs inside Gainbridge Fieldhouse. It's the clearest overlap of school music and basketball in the state.

moments.name: Indy 500 race weekend (Carb Day concert, Snake Pit, 'Back Home Again in Indiana')
moments.why: The state's biggest communal music moment: 300,000-plus people go silent for "Back Home Again" before the green flag.

moments.name: Bill Monroe's Bean Blossom Bluegrass Festival
moments.why: Running since 1967 in Brown County, it's a pilgrimage to rural Indiana's acoustic roots.

moments.name: Indy Jazz Fest
moments.why: The city's jazz showcase, and the logical summer stage for an Avenue-heritage preview.

moments.name: Indiana Black Expo Summer Celebration
moments.why: Black Indy's biggest annual gathering since 1971, with concerts. The right launch window for an Avenue capsule made with Black Indy creators.

moments.name: DCI World Championships
moments.why: The world's top drum corps take over Lucas Oil Stadium and downtown, a ready-made audience for a drumline-inspired preseason drop.

moments.name: Pacers home opener: Haliburton's return
moments.why: Haliburton's first Fieldhouse game back from his Achilles tear is the "Back Home Again" night.

moments.name: Marching November: ISSMA state finals, BOA Grand Nationals and PASIC
moments.why: Indiana's band families and the global percussion world converge downtown in the season's first weeks. Perfect for a Fieldhouse drumline night.

vocabulary.meaning: A jazz-era nickname for Indianapolis, worn with pride in Black Indy and local hip-hop. It's affectionate from insiders, so let local creators lead.
Indiana Avenue, the historic Black business and jazz district northwest of downtown.
Slick Leonard's radio call for a Pacers three, still shouted by fans and used by the team.
Shorthand for "Back Home Again in Indiana," the song sung before the Indy 500 and the state's emotional anthem.
What locals still call Ruoff Music Center, the Noblesville amphitheater, decades after the name changed.
The Friday before the Indy 500: final practice, pit-stop competition and a big infield concert.
The EDM festival inside Turn 3 of the Speedway on race day, and Indiana's biggest dance-music crowd.
"South of Broad Ripple," the College Ave strip that's home to the Jazz Kitchen and Luna Music.

designCues.cue: Walker terra cotta: the warm fired-clay color of the Avenue's 1927 theatre
designCues.source: The terra-cotta facade and Africanesque Art Deco ornament of the Madam Walker Legacy Center on Indiana Avenue.
designCues.use: Use it as a base or accent beside Pacers navy for an Avenue capsule made with the Center. Take the color only. The ornament and African-derived motifs are off limits unless the Center partners and is credited. The hex is approximate, so lab-match it.

designCues.cue: Sousaphone brass: a darker, metallic counterpart to Pacers gold
designCues.source: The brass lines of Indiana marching bands and the drum corps that fill Lucas Oil every August.
designCues.use: Use it for metal hardware, foil prints, aglets and zipper pulls beside Pacers gold (#FDBB30) for a brass-and-gold tone-on-tone. It's approximate, so match it with a metallic lab dip.

designCues.cue: Octaves: two parallel lines a fixed interval apart
designCues.source: Wes Montgomery's thumb-picked octave technique, the signature sound of Indianapolis jazz.
designCues.use: Run it as a double pinstripe, sleeve taping or side-panel piping. It's an abstract nod that needs no likeness, but naming Wes on product requires his estate's license.

designCues.cue: Drum-corps band jacket: high collar, asymmetric sash panel, gauntlet cuffs
designCues.source: DCI and Bands of America uniforms, centered on Lucas Oil Stadium each August and November.
designCues.use: Turn it into a warmup jacket or shooting shirt with a diagonal sash panel and oversized ribbed gauntlet cuffs. Never copy a specific corps' or school's uniform.

designCues.cue: 1917 sheet-music script for "Back Home Again in Indiana"
designCues.source: The original public-domain sheet music of the Indy 500's pre-race song.
designCues.use: Redraw the lettering for a "Back Home Again" chest or neck lockup on home-opener product. Keep it apart from Indy 500 marks, checkered flags and the wing-and-wheel.

designCues.cue: Cassette J-card track list of Pacers moments
designCues.source: The Moments Mixtape City Edition, plus moments fans would put on it. Those are the ABA titles ('70, '72, '73), Reggie's 8 points in 8.9 seconds at MSG (1995) and Haliburton's 2025 Finals Game 1 winner.
designCues.use: Print it on hangtags, inside necks and jacket linings as a "Side A / Side B" track list. Check the official uniform design first, so the extension matches it without duplicating it.

designCues.source: Gennett Records in Richmond, where King Oliver's band with Louis Armstrong and Hoagy Carmichael ("Stardust") first recorded.
designCues.use: Use a fine concentric groove emboss on patches or hangtags for a statewide heritage story. Tell it only with Gennett's full history in mind (see watchouts).

productHooks: A "Back Home Again" home-opener capsule for late October 2026. It's a shooting shirt and tee in the returning Moments Mixtape white, royal and gold, with the public-domain 1917 lyric in sheet-music script. Frame it as the team's return, not as Haliburton signature product.
A Moments Mixtape "Side B" lifestyle drop: cassette J-card hangtags, an inside-neck track list and a launch mix commissioned from Indy DJs and producers. Sell it as a numbered run at Luna Music.

A drumline warmup pack with a band-jacket warmup, gauntlet cuffs and sousaphone-brass hardware. Debut it in the November marching weeks, with an Indiana high-school drumline playing a Fieldhouse game and proceeds going to Music for All band programs.

An Avenue capsule co-designed with the Madam Walker Legacy Center and Black Indy artists, in Walker terra cotta, navy and octave stripes. Launch it at Indiana Black Expo Summer Celebration in July, with a revenue share to the Center.
A "Boom Baby!" three-point tee with a sound-on QR to Slick Leonard's archival call. Release it after a Pacers three-point milestone night, subject to clearance from the team and Leonard's estate.
watchouts: Brand conflict: Haliburton signed with Puma in Oct 2024 (signature-line naming unconfirmed). Keep anything celebrating his return team-level, use only NBA-licensed player assets, and keep "Hali" naming off Nike product.

Indiana Avenue is Black heritage shaped by displacement. Urban renewal, I-65 and the IUPUI campus cleared much of the near-westside. Co-create with the Madam Walker Legacy Center, the Crispus Attucks Museum and Black Indy artists, and pay them. Don't borrow jazz-age imagery.

IP and clearance: The Speedway owns the Indy 500, Carb Day, Snake Pit, checkered-flag and wing-and-wheel marks. Recordings of "Back Home Again" (Nabors' included) are copyrighted even though the 1917 song is not. Corps and school uniforms belong to their organizations. The names, likenesses and lyrics of Wes Montgomery, Babyface and Mellencamp all need licensing.

Gennett Records also pressed private Ku Klux Klan records in the 1920s, when the Klan dominated Indiana politics. Use its jazz story only with that history in mind, and never as unexamined "Indiana heritage" nostalgia.

Swap risk and currency: cornfields-and-barns heartland imagery is generic and can caricature rural Indiana. Anchor small-town cues in named Indiana songs and pep bands. Reconfirm venue names, festival dates and the current hip-hop scene before acting, because this dossier is from model knowledge.

sources.title: Pacers bringing back 'Moments Mixtape' City Edition uniform for 2026-27 (Roundtable)

verify: Confirm Haliburton is still with Puma and whether a signature line exists for 2026-27. That decides whether Nike can build on his return beyond team-level product.
Confirm the Pacers' 2026-27 home-opener date, and whether the team plans a return-night theme for Haliburton.
Check the Moments Mixtape uniform's actual design details (any track-list or cassette motifs) and its 2026-27 City Edition game nights, so extensions match rather than duplicate.
Find out who runs Pacers in-arena music now: the Fieldhouse DJ, PA voice, anthem singers and any local-artist halftime or walkout partnerships.
Identify the current Naptown hip-hop and R&B artists, producers and DJs locals rep, and any with real ties to Pacers players (not named in this dossier).
Confirm the Madam Walker Legacy Center and Crispus Attucks Museum are operating, and ask about their current programming and openness to a co-created capsule.
Check the dates for DCI World Championships at Lucas Oil Stadium in August 2027, and for ISSMA state finals, BOA Grand Nationals and PASIC in Indianapolis in November 2026.
Check Indy Jazz Fest's 2027 month and dates, and the Indiana Black Expo Summer Celebration's July 2027 dates and concert lineup.
Confirm the IHSAA boys' basketball state finals at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in March 2027.
Confirm the Jazz Kitchen, Chatterbox Jazz Club, HI-FI Indy, the Vogue, Luna Music and Rhythm! Discovery Center are all still open under the same names.
Find the clearance owners for "Boom Baby!" audio (the team or radio rights holder, and Leonard's estate) and for Wes Montgomery's name and likeness.
Confirm Babyface's and Mellencamp's current availability to collaborate, and any existing ties to the Pacers or competing apparel brands.
